trust_decision.summary: A module loader decides whether the file-supplied channel and pattern counts give a track count (numchn*numpat) that fits the UWORD of.numtrk used to size of.tracks in AllocTracks. The loop that fills tracks indexes up to numchn*numpat. In DSM_Load this check is missing.

landing_point.why: The summary names the DSM loader and an integer overflow. The only multiplication in DSM_Load header handling is of.numtrk=of.numchn*of.numpat.

fix_sites.entry_point: Player_Load / Player_LoadFP / Player_LoadMem / Player_LoadGeneric (libmikmod/playercode/mloader.c:641-683) -> Player_LoadGeneric_internal -> load_dsm.Load (DSM_Load)
fix_sites.module_kind: format loader (file parser) in the library core

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report and fix are about the DSM loader only. OKT is a different format with its own chunk parser, it has at most 8 channels, and the multiplication sits inside the pattern-body handler rather than the header code, so a solver can say 'other formats were not reported'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Valid DSM files with up to 16 channels and normal pattern counts must still load. A shared guard in AllocTracks/AllocPatterns that rejects large legitimate products, or a DSM channel cap below 16, would break real modules. Formats such as ULT legitimately reach 255*256=65280 tracks, which is near the UWORD limit.

O6_input_shapes: numchn > DSM_MAXCHAN (16), which also prevents dsmbuf[t*64] reading past the 16*64 buffer
numchn*numpat > 65535 (the UWORD numtrk wraps, so of.tracks is undersized)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: OKT loader: numpat is a raw file UWORD (SLEN chunk) and numchn is 4-8 (CMOD). of.numtrk=numpat*numchn is never bounded, so it wraps, and PBOD writes of.tracks[patnum*numchn+i].
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a different format and file from the advisory, the channel count is small (<=8), and the product is computed lazily inside OKT_doPBOD rather than in the header code.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another file in the same loaders/ dir (load_okt.c:286, 312 vs load_dsm.c:273)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: XM already casts (UWORD)numpat*numchn. Dropping or loosening the numpat<=256 / numchn<=64 header bounds (load_xm.c:681,686) would create a sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Those header bounds are the only thing keeping the product small. A maintainer relaxing them for modern trackers with more patterns is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: AMF takes numtrk from numorders*numchannels or from the file's numtracks. Widening numorders to a UWORD (newer AMF versions) would create a wrap.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The header fields are versioned. A version bump that reads a wider field is a natural change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: IT patnum is capped at 255. Raising the cap (OpenMPT IT files allow more patterns) with 64 channels would still fit, but adding extended channel handling could overflow.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Format extensions push these caps upward.

O9_family: CWE-190 integer overflow (UWORD truncation of a count product) leading to an undersized heap allocation and an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake or autotools, any C compiler. The no-sound driver is enough for loading.
O10_build.project_tests: None for loaders. libmikmod/examples/test/test.c is only an example program. Tests would load crafted modules through Player_LoadMem with the nosound driver.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a numchn*numpat>65535 bail-out in DSM_Load only (omitting the numchn>16 cap that dsmbuf needs), leaving OKT's identical wrap open.

out_of_scope_notes: libmikmod/loaders/load_dsm.c:290 sanity check tests of.positions[t] (still zero from calloc, mloader.c:188) instead of 'order', so order indices above numpat are not rejected. This is a different protection (position bounds).
libmikmod/loaders/load_dsm.c:337 ignores the DSM_ReadPattern return value.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell). libmikmod is a small C library, likely under 5 MB of source, which would make tiny_repo apply. That flag is not set because the size is unmeasured.
present_in_latest for the OKT route is unknown (no latest release given).

ULT (load_ult.c:213-215): the worst case is 255*256=65280, which fits a UWORD. noc=255 makes numchn 0, so AllocPatterns rejects it. Judged not a route, based on the UBYTE type of of.numchn only (the noc variable's declared type was not re-read).

Other loaders (xm, it, s3m, imf, stx, stm, mod, m15, gdm, far, asy, amf, 669, med) appear bounded by header caps or UBYTE fields. This was checked by grep of the caps, not by full reading of each loader.
